views.purpose: The module-decomposition viewpoint answers the questions by displaying the main modules and subsystems owning the seat booking functionality, their responsibilities, interactions, and affected surrounding parts.
required_evidence: modules or subsystems that own the seat booking functionality
surrounding parts of the system that depend on or are affected by seat booking modifications
views.diagram_language_rule: viewpoint agent chose plantuml: PlantUML can cleanly represent modules, subsystems, and their containment or uses relationships for the seat booking functionality.

notes: Eligible because they frame the chosen concerns: module-decomposition, context, cnc-runtime, code-mapping

Context was rejected because it focuses on boundary actors and datastores rather than internal modules and maintainability; cnc-runtime was rejected because it emphasizes runtime components and connectors rather than static module ownership and dependencies; code-mapping was rejected because it maps to implementing types and risks a detailed class dump instead of focusing on high-level module decomposition.
diagram language plantuml: viewpoint agent chose plantuml: PlantUML can cleanly represent modules, subsystems, and their containment or uses relationships for the seat booking functionality.
